what_they_did: The author compared sign images from the Indus script, proto-cuneiform and proto-Elamite with signs from newer Dongba, old Naxi and a mixed Tibetan-Yi corridor set of Ba-Shu, Classical Yi and old Naxi signs (section 3.1).
She trained contrastive CNN-Swin image encoders with an NT-Xent loss at temperature 0.1 (section 3.5).
For each target script she trained five models, fifteen in all, each in its own embedding space (section 3.4, Table 3.1).
She compared glyph-level and script-level cosine similarity between the target scripts and the corridor set.
what_they_found: Mean glyph-level cosine similarity with the corridor set is 0.635 for Indus, 0.102 for proto-cuneiform and 0.078 for proto-Elamite (Table 4.1, p. 31).
Script-level similarity is 0.930 for Indus (interval 0.917 to 0.942), 0.887 for proto-cuneiform and 0.855 for proto-Elamite (section 4.1.1).
Effect sizes (Cohen's d) are 7.13 to 8.36, which the author says are inflated by low variance (Table 4.3; section 5.1.1).
Several ensemble members stopped at epoch 1, and validation losses lie roughly between 8.7 and 10.2 (Table 3.1, pp. 23-24).
The author lists independent origin, common ancestry and convergent evolution as alternative explanations (section 5.4).
strength_and_limits: The code is public (github.com/oohalakkadi/ivc2tyc, section 6.3) and the author is open about inflated effect sizes.
Similarities from separate embedding spaces, trained per target script, cannot be compared across target scripts.
Several models barely trained, so the embeddings may reflect image style more than sign form.
Our own red-team run found the Indus advantage disappears when the Ba-Shu signs are removed (experiments/redteam_ivc2tyc).

authors_next.idea: Study Tibetan rock art and archaeology along the Shu-Shendu road.
Add linguistic and semantic constraints to the embeddings and include more Central and East Asian scripts as controls.

ideas_for_us.idea: Retrain one shared embedding space on all scripts together, then compare Indus-to-corridor similarity against a null of shuffled script labels and against unrelated control scripts drawn in a similar style.
ideas_for_us.why: This removes the cross-space comparison that makes the published numbers incomparable.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: The ivc2tyc code and sign images (public), plus open sign images for several unrelated control scripts.

ideas_for_us.idea: Report the corridor similarity sign by sign and check whether the Indus advantage comes from a handful of simple shapes such as strokes, circles and crosses.
ideas_for_us.why: Simple geometric signs recur in unrelated scripts and could drive the result alone.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: The ivc2tyc repository outputs and our existing red-team run.
